name: Peppermint
source_reference: ISO 856:2006 - Oil of peppermint; Lawrence, 'Mint: The Genus Mentha', 2007; Arctander, 'Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin', 1960
notes: Willamette Valley (Oregon) peppermint is considered the highest quality. Indian (Mentha arvensis) dementholized mint is distinct and cheaper. Pulegone content must be monitored for safety.

key_markers.2216-51-5: Menthol - cooling, fresh mint character; primary olfactive driver
key_markers.89-80-5: Menthone - minty-green ketone providing body and depth
key_markers.494-90-6: Menthofuran - sweet, musty, hay-like; quality marker (high levels indicate late-harvest or re-distilled oil)

olfactive_description: Intensely cool, fresh, and penetrating minty-green with a clean, sweet undertone. Invigorating with camphoraceous-herbaceous body. Sweet menthyl acetate adds a fruity-candy facet.
